title.en: Obligation, Advice and Prohibition (should, must, have to)
title.es: Obligación, consejo y prohibición (should, must, have to)

text.en: Modal verbs are always followed by the base verb, without to (except ought to). There are three main questions: what do I advise (should, ought to, had better), what is required (must, have to), what is forbidden (mustn’t), and what is not necessary (don’t have to). The biggest trap: the Spanish “no tienes que” is don’t have to (it is not necessary), but “no debes” is mustn’t (it is forbidden), and the two mean completely different things.
text.es: Después de los verbos modales siempre va el verbo base, sin to (excepto ought to). Hay cuatro preguntas principales: qué aconsejo (should, ought to, had better), qué es obligatorio (must, have to), qué está prohibido (mustn’t) y qué no es necesario (don’t have to). La trampa más grande: «no tienes que» es don’t have to (no hace falta), pero «no debes» es mustn’t (está prohibido), y las dos significan cosas totalmente distintas.

text.en: Should + base verb: advice, opinion. Negative: shouldn’t. Ought to is similar but more formal: “You ought to see a doctor.”
text.es: Should + verbo base: consejo, opinión. Negación: shouldn’t. Ought to es parecido pero más formal: «You ought to see a doctor.»

examples.es: You look tired. You should go to bed early.

tr.en: You look tired. You should go to bed early.
tr.es: Te ves cansado. Deberías acostarte temprano.

examples.es: You shouldn't eat so much sugar.

tr.en: You shouldn't eat so much sugar.
tr.es: No deberías comer tanta azúcar.

text.en: Had better + base verb: strong advice or a warning; if you don’t, there will be a problem. It looks past but refers to the present or future. Negative: had better not.
text.es: Had better + verbo base: consejo fuerte o advertencia; si no lo haces, habrá un problema. Parece pasado pero se refiere al presente o al futuro. Negación: had better not.

examples.es: You had better hurry, or you will miss the bus.

tr.en: You had better hurry, or you will miss the bus.
tr.es: Más vale que te apures, o vas a perder el camión.

tr.en: You'd better not be late.
tr.es: Más vale que no llegues tarde.

text.en: Must or have to + base verb: required. Have to is conjugated (he has to), and questions and negatives need do: Does she have to wear glasses?
text.es: Must o have to + verbo base: obligatorio. Have to se conjuga (he has to), y las preguntas y negaciones necesitan do: Does she have to wear glasses?

examples.es: I have to get up early tomorrow.

tr.en: I have to get up early tomorrow.
tr.es: Mañana tengo que levantarme temprano.

examples.es: Does she have to wear glasses?

tr.en: Does she have to wear glasses?
tr.es: ¿Tiene que usar lentes?

text.en: Mustn’t = forbidden. Don’t have to = not necessary, not required, but you may. The two cannot be swapped.
text.es: Mustn’t = prohibido. Don’t have to = no es necesario, no es obligatorio, pero puedes. Los dos no se pueden cambiar.

examples.es: You mustn't use your phone during the exam.

tr.en: You mustn't use your phone during the exam.
tr.es: No debes usar tu celular durante el examen.

examples.es: You don't have to wear a uniform.

tr.en: You don't have to wear a uniform.
tr.es: No tienes que usar uniforme.

text.en: Past: must has no past form, so use had to: “Yesterday I had to work late.” Questions and negatives with did: Did you have to…? I didn’t have to…
text.es: Pasado: must no tiene forma de pasado, así que se usa had to: «Yesterday I had to work late.» Preguntas y negaciones con did: Did you have to…? I didn’t have to…

examples.es: Yesterday I had to work late.

tr.en: Yesterday I had to work late.
tr.es: Ayer tuve que trabajar hasta tarde.

tr.en: We didn't have to pay.
tr.es: No tuvimos que pagar.

title.en: B1 extras: the past, unnecessary, expected

text.en: Advice or criticism about the past: should have / ought to have / shouldn’t have + participle. It says what you should (or should not) have done.
text.es: Consejo o crítica sobre el pasado: should have / ought to have / shouldn’t have + participio. Dice lo que se debió (o no se debió) hacer.

tr.en: You should have called me.
tr.es: Debiste haberme llamado.

tr.en: We shouldn't have waited.
tr.es: No debimos haber esperado.

text.en: Needn’t + base verb: not necessary (= don’t have to). Needn’t have + participle: what you did was unnecessary, but it happened.
text.es: Needn’t + verbo base: no es necesario (= don’t have to). Needn’t have + participio: lo que hiciste era innecesario, pero pasó.

tr.en: You needn't wait.
tr.es: No hace falta que esperes.

tr.en: You needn't have come.
tr.es: No hacía falta que vinieras.

text.en: Be supposed to: according to a plan, a rule or an expectation. Have got to: informal have to. Be allowed to: permission (in the past: was / wasn’t allowed to).
text.es: Be supposed to: según un plan, una regla o una expectativa. Have got to: have to informal. Be allowed to: permiso (en el pasado: was / wasn’t allowed to).

examples.es: The meeting is supposed to start at nine.

tr.en: The meeting is supposed to start at nine.
tr.es: Se supone que la reunión empieza a las nueve.

examples.es: I have got to go now.

tr.en: I have got to go now.
tr.es: Tengo que irme ahora.

text.en: The Spanish “no tienes que venir” is “You don’t have to come” (you don’t need to), not “You mustn’t come” (you are forbidden). Mustn’t expresses a prohibition, don’t have to only says it is not necessary.
text.es: El «no tienes que venir» del español es «You don’t have to come» (no hace falta), no «You mustn’t come» (está prohibido). Mustn’t expresa una prohibición, don’t have to solo dice que no es necesario.

text.en: After a modal verb there is no to and no -s: not “You should to go” and not “She musts go”, but “You should go”, “She must go”. In questions the modal verb goes first: Should I wear a tie?
text.es: Después de un verbo modal no hay to ni -s: no «You should to go» ni «She musts go», sino «You should go», «She must go». En las preguntas el verbo modal va primero: Should I wear a tie?

text.en: Had better looks past but does not mean the past: “You had better hurry” = hurry now. For the past use had to: “I had to hurry.”
text.es: Had better parece pasado pero no significa pasado: «You had better hurry» = apúrate ahora. Para el pasado se usa had to: «I had to hurry.»

speak.en: After modal verbs the base verb always follows, without «to». «Should» gives advice: «You should see a doctor». «Had better» is a strong warning: «You had better hurry». «Must» and «have to» mean required: «I have to get up early». «Mustn't» means forbidden: «You mustn't park here». «Don't have to», in contrast, means not necessary: «You don't have to come». These two are not the same. «Must» has no past form, so «had to» is used: «Yesterday I had to work late». For advice about the past use «should have» plus the participle: «You should have called me».
speak.es: Después de los verbos modales siempre va el verbo base, sin «to». «Should» da un consejo: «You should see a doctor». «Had better» es una advertencia fuerte: «You had better hurry». «Must» y «have to» significan obligatorio: «I have to get up early». «Mustn't» significa prohibido: «You mustn't park here». «Don't have to», en cambio, significa que no es necesario: «You don't have to come». Estos dos no son lo mismo. «Must» no tiene forma de pasado, así que se usa «had to»: «Yesterday I had to work late». Para un consejo sobre el pasado se usa «should have» más el participio: «You should have called me».

items.sentence: You look tired. You ___ go to bed early.

why.en: Advice: should + base verb. The tiredness is visible, so going to bed early is good advice.
why.es: Consejo: should + verbo base. El cansancio se nota, por eso acostarse temprano es un buen consejo.

must to.en: After must there is no to; “must to” is an incorrect form.
must to.es: Después de must no hay to; «must to» es una forma incorrecta.

are should.en: Should stands alone, without the verb be; “are should” does not exist.
are should.es: Should va solo, sin el verbo be; «are should» no existe.

tr.en: You look tired. You should go to bed early.
tr.es: Te ves cansado. Deberías irte a dormir temprano.

items.sentence: I made a mistake. I ___ have listened to you.

why.en: Regret or advice about the past: should have + participle.
why.es: Arrepentimiento o consejo sobre el pasado: should have + participio.

can.en: “Can have listened” does not express regret; “should have” means “I ought to have”.
can.es: «Can have listened» no expresa arrepentimiento; «should have» significa «debí haber».

am.en: “Am have listened” is not a possible structure; before have you need a modal verb (should have).
am.es: «Am have listened» no es una estructura posible; antes de have hace falta un verbo modal (should have).

examples: We should have left at six.

tr.en: I made a mistake. I should have listened to you.
tr.es: Cometí un error. Debí haberte escuchado.

items.sentence: You ___ come with us. It is not necessary.

why.en: Not necessary: needn’t + base verb (it means don’t have to).
why.es: No es necesario: needn’t + verbo base (significa don’t have to).

mustn't.en: Mustn’t is a prohibition; the sentence only says it is not necessary to come.
mustn't.es: Mustn’t es una prohibición; la oración solo dice que no es necesario venir.

can't.en: Can’t would mean he cannot come; the sentence says it is just not required.
can't.es: Can’t significaría que no puede venir; la oración dice que solo no es obligatorio.

tr.en: You needn't come with us. It is not necessary.
tr.es: No hace falta que vengas con nosotros. No es necesario.

items.sentence: The meeting is ___ to start at nine.

why.en: Be supposed to means that according to the plan or the rule it should happen: is supposed to start.
why.es: Be supposed to significa que según el plan o la regla debe pasar: is supposed to start.

suppose.en: In be supposed to the participle is used (supposed), not the base verb.
suppose.es: En be supposed to se usa el participio (supposed), no el verbo base.

supposing.en: The -ing form does not fit here: the structure is be + supposed + to.
supposing.es: La forma -ing no encaja aquí: la estructura es be + supposed + to.

examples: The train is supposed to arrive at six.
We are supposed to wait here.

tr.en: The meeting is supposed to start at nine.
tr.es: Se supone que la reunión empieza a las nueve.

items.sentence: I have ___ to go now. My mother is waiting.

why.en: Have got to means “must” and is informal: I have got to go (= I have to go).
why.es: Have got to significa «tener que» y es informal: I have got to go (= I have to go).

get.en: “Have get to” does not exist; in have got to the form got is used.
get.es: «Have get to» no existe; en have got to se usa la forma got.

going.en: “Have going to” is incorrect; in have got to the form got is used.
going.es: «Have going to» es incorrecto; en have got to se usa la forma got.

tr.en: I have got to go now. My mother is waiting.
tr.es: Me tengo que ir ahora. Mi mamá me está esperando.

why.en: After ought comes to: ought to + base verb.
why.es: Después de ought va to: ought to + verbo base.

for.en: “Ought for” does not exist; ought always goes with to.
for.es: «Ought for» no existe; ought siempre va con to.

that.en: “Ought that” does not exist; the structure for advice is ought to + base verb.
that.es: «Ought that» no existe; la estructura del consejo es ought to + verbo base.

tr.en: You ought to see a doctor.
tr.es: Deberías ver a un médico.

items.sentence: You ___ better hurry or you will miss the bus.

why.en: Strong advice, a warning: had better + base verb.
why.es: Consejo fuerte, advertencia: had better + verbo base.

have.en: “Have better” is not an existing structure; a warning needs had better.
have.es: «Have better» no es una estructura que exista; una advertencia necesita had better.

would.en: “Would better” is not an existing structure; the correct one is had better, or would rather with a different meaning.
would.es: «Would better» no es una estructura que exista; la correcta es had better, o would rather con otro significado.

tr.en: You had better hurry or you will miss the bus.
tr.es: Más vale que te apures o perderás el camión.

why.en: After should comes the base verb, without to: should drink.
why.es: Después de should va el verbo base, sin to: should drink.

to drink.en: After should there is no to; “should to drink” is incorrect.
to drink.es: Después de should no hay to; «should to drink» es incorrecto.

drinking.en: After should comes the base verb, not an -ing form.
drinking.es: Después de should viene el verbo base, no una forma -ing.

tr.en: You should drink more water.
tr.es: Deberías beber más agua.

items.sentence: ___ I wear a tie to the interview?

why.en: In a question the modal verb goes first: Should I wear a tie…?
why.es: En una pregunta el verbo modal va primero: Should I wear a tie…?

Do should.en: Modal verbs do not take do; “Do should I” is incorrect.
Do should.es: Los verbos modales no llevan do; «Do should I» es incorrecto.

Am.en: “Am I wear” is incorrect; after Am an -ing form would follow (Am I wearing…?), which means something else.
Am.es: «Am I wear» es incorrecto; después de Am iría una forma -ing (Am I wearing…?), que significa otra cosa.

tr.en: Should I wear a tie to the interview?
tr.es: ¿Debería usar corbata para la entrevista?

items.sentence: You ___ have said that. It was not good.

why.en: Criticism about the past: shouldn’t have + participle (you ought not to have).
why.es: Crítica sobre el pasado: shouldn’t have + participio (no debiste).

mustn't.en: “Mustn’t have” is not used for criticism about the past; “you shouldn’t have” is the form.
mustn't.es: «Mustn’t have» no se usa para criticar el pasado; la forma es «you shouldn’t have».

don't.en: “Don’t have said” is not possible; criticism about the past takes shouldn’t have + participle.
don't.es: «Don’t have said» no es posible; la crítica sobre el pasado lleva shouldn’t have + participio.

tr.en: You shouldn't have said that. It was not good.
tr.es: No debiste haber dicho eso. No estuvo bien.

items.sentence: We ought to have ___ at six.

why.en: Advice about the past: ought to have + participle (the same as should have).
why.es: Consejo sobre el pasado: ought to have + participio (igual que should have).

leave.en: After have you need the participle (left), not the base verb.
leave.es: Después de have hace falta el participio (left), no el verbo base.

leaving.en: After have you need the participle (left), not the -ing form.
leaving.es: Después de have hace falta el participio (left), no la forma -ing.

tr.en: We ought to have left at six.
tr.es: Debimos haber salido a las seis.

items.sentence: You should ___ eat so much sugar.

why.en: The negative of should is should not (shouldn’t): you should not eat.
why.es: La negación de should es should not (shouldn’t): you should not eat.

don't.en: Modal verbs do not take do; “should don’t” is incorrect.
don't.es: Los verbos modales no llevan do; «should don’t» es incorrecto.

no.en: “Should no eat” is a word-for-word copy of the Spanish “no deberías comer”; in English you need not.
no.es: «Should no eat» es una copia palabra por palabra del «no deberías comer»; en inglés hace falta not.

tr.en: You should not eat so much sugar.
tr.es: No deberías comer tanta azúcar.

items.sentence: People ___ to take photos in the museum.

why.en: A rule: aren’t allowed to + base verb (not permitted).
why.es: Una regla: aren’t allowed to + verbo base (no permitido).

don't allow.en: “Don’t allow” is active (someone doesn’t permit); the rule needs the passive form: aren’t allowed.
don't allow.es: «Don’t allow» es activo (alguien no permite); la regla necesita la forma pasiva: aren’t allowed.

not allowed.en: “Not allowed” without the verb be is incomplete; the sentence needs aren’t.
not allowed.es: «Not allowed» sin el verbo be está incompleto; la oración necesita aren’t.

examples: You are not allowed to park here.

tr.en: People aren't allowed to take photos in the museum.
tr.es: No se permite tomar fotos en el museo.

items.sentence: We took umbrellas, but we ___ have. It did not rain.

why.en: It was unnecessary but it happened: needn’t have + participle.
why.es: Era innecesario y aun así pasó: needn’t have + participio.

mustn't.en: “Mustn’t have” is not used here; for an unnecessary past action use needn’t have.
mustn't.es: «Mustn’t have» no se usa aquí; para una acción pasada innecesaria se usa needn’t have.

haven't.en: “Haven’t have” is incorrect; before have you need a modal verb (needn’t have).
haven't.es: «Haven’t have» es incorrecto; antes de have hace falta un verbo modal (needn’t have).

tr.en: We took umbrellas, but we needn't have. It did not rain.
tr.es: Llevamos sombrillas, pero no fue necesario. No llovió.

items.sentence: When I was a child, I ___ allowed to go out late.

why.en: Permission in the past: was / wasn’t allowed to.
why.es: Permiso en el pasado: was / wasn’t allowed to.

didn't.en: After didn’t you need the base verb (didn’t allow); “allowed to” goes with the verb be.
didn't.es: Después de didn’t hace falta el verbo base (didn’t allow); «allowed to» va con el verbo be.

aren't.en: Aren’t is for the plural and the present; the sentence is in the past and with I you need wasn’t.
aren't.es: Aren’t es para el plural y el presente; la oración está en pasado y con I hace falta wasn’t.

tr.en: When I was a child, I wasn't allowed to go out late.
tr.es: Cuando era niño, no me dejaban salir hasta tarde.

items.sentence: We ___ have to pay. It was free.

why.en: Past “it was not necessary”: didn’t have to + base verb.
why.es: El «no hacía falta» del pasado: didn’t have to + verbo base.

don't.en: Don’t is present; the sentence is in the past (was free).
don't.es: Don’t es presente; la oración está en pasado (was free).

won't.en: Won’t means the future; the sentence is in the past (was free), so you need didn’t have to.
won't.es: Won’t significa futuro; la oración está en pasado (was free), por eso hace falta didn’t have to.

tr.en: We didn't have to pay. It was free.
tr.es: No tuvimos que pagar. Fue gratis.

items.sentence: You ___ better not be late again.

why.en: A negative warning: had better not + base verb.
why.es: Una advertencia en negativo: had better not + verbo base.

have.en: “Have better not” does not exist; the form of the warning is had better not.
have.es: «Have better not» no existe; la forma de la advertencia es had better not.

would.en: “Would better not” is not an existing structure; you need had better not.
would.es: «Would better not» no es una estructura que exista; hace falta had better not.

tr.en: You had better not be late again.
tr.es: Más vale que no vuelvas a llegar tarde.

tr.en: You should see a doctor.
tr.es: Deberías ir al doctor.

text.en: obligation: there is no choice
text.es: obligación: no hay otra opción

wrong.en: Should does not express an obligation but advice; for an obligation use must or have to.
wrong.es: Should no expresa una obligación sino un consejo; para una obligación se usa must o have to.

text.en: advice, an opinion
text.es: consejo, una opinión

text.en: prohibition: not allowed
text.es: prohibición: no se permite

wrong.en: Should does not forbid anything; mustn’t is for a prohibition.
wrong.es: Should no prohíbe nada; mustn’t es para la prohibición.

tr.en: You should have called me.
tr.es: Debiste haberme llamado.

text.en: advice about the future
text.es: un consejo sobre el futuro

wrong.en: Should + base verb is advice about the future; should have + participle refers to the past (ought to have).
wrong.es: Should + verbo base es un consejo sobre el futuro; should have + participio se refiere al pasado (debió).

text.en: criticism or regret about the past: should have + participle
text.es: crítica o arrepentimiento sobre el pasado: should have + participio

text.en: obligation: must
text.es: obligación: must

wrong.en: Should does not express an obligation but advice or criticism; for an obligation use must / have to.
wrong.es: Should no expresa una obligación sino un consejo o una crítica; para una obligación se usa must / have to.

tr.en: We needn't have hurried.
tr.es: No hacía falta que nos apuráramos (y lo hicimos).

text.en: prohibition: we were not allowed to
text.es: prohibición: no se nos permitía

wrong.en: Needn’t have is not a prohibition: it says it was not necessary, but it happened.
wrong.es: Needn’t have no es una prohibición: dice que no hacía falta, pero pasó.

text.en: it was unnecessary but it happened: needn’t have + participle
text.es: era innecesario y aun así pasó: needn’t have + participio

text.en: it was a mistake: shouldn’t have + participle
text.es: fue un error: shouldn’t have + participio

wrong.en: Shouldn’t have criticizes a mistake; needn’t have only says it was not needed.
wrong.es: Shouldn’t have critica un error; needn’t have solo dice que no hacía falta.

items.es: The meeting is supposed to start at nine.

tr.en: The meeting is supposed to start at nine.
tr.es: Se supone que la reunión empieza a las nueve.

text.en: obligation: must
text.es: obligación: must

wrong.en: Be supposed to is not a strict obligation but a plan or an expectation; for an obligation use must / have to.
wrong.es: Be supposed to no es una obligación estricta sino un plan o una expectativa; para una obligación se usa must / have to.

text.en: according to the plan or the rule it should happen: be supposed to
text.es: según el plan o la regla debe pasar: be supposed to

text.en: a past habit: used to
text.es: un hábito del pasado: used to

wrong.en: Supposed to does not mean a habit but a plan or an expectation; a habit takes used to.
wrong.es: Supposed to no significa un hábito sino un plan o una expectativa; un hábito lleva used to.

tr.en: You had better hurry.
tr.es: Más vale que te apures.

text.en: past perfect: an earlier event
text.es: pasado perfecto: un hecho anterior

wrong.en: After had better comes the base verb (hurry), not a participle; the sentence is a warning about now.
wrong.es: Después de had better va el verbo base (hurry), no un participio; la oración es una advertencia sobre ahora.

text.en: a past obligation: had to
text.es: una obligación en el pasado: had to

wrong.en: Had to is a past obligation, had better is strong advice about the present or future.
wrong.es: Had to es una obligación en el pasado, had better es un consejo fuerte sobre el presente o el futuro.

text.en: strong advice, a warning: had better
text.es: consejo fuerte, advertencia: had better

pairs.es: Se supone que la reunión empieza a las nueve.
pairs.en: The meeting is supposed to start at nine.
